newsitem.title: USA: High Plains Wheat - Basis falters as harvest rolls.
newsitem.headline: High Plains Wheat - Basis falters as harvest rolls.

text.p: Basis bids for hard red winter wheat weakened Wednesday at scattered locations across the U.S. Plains as harvesting rolled on in northern Texas, grain merchandisers said.
One Oklahoma dealer said his firm took in 45 truckloads of new crop wheat earlier this week from around the Fort Worth, Texas area.
"It's probably the best quality stuff we've seen out of Texas in the last five years," the Oklahoma dealer said. "Test weights were good. It's just good, heavy number one or two wheat."
Another dealer in Kansas said that although protein levels were erratic on one group of samples from Texas he had seen, the test weights were high.
"Protein ranged from 10 (percent) all the way up to 17.3. But test weights were pretty strong at 58.8 to 63.5 (lbs)," the dealer said.
Basis values in cents/bu against KCBT wheat, cash=dollars/bu.
(Note: N=KCBT July. unq- unquoted, na - not applicable)
